title: NCLT Kolkata Admits Shevin Capital Services Into Insolvency Over Rs 1.15 Crore Default
case_name: Aryan Mining and Trading Corporation Private Limited v. Shevin Capital Services Private Limited
citation: C.P.(IB) No. 54/KB/2026 (Section 7, Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016)
card_summary: NCLT Kolkata admitted a Section 7 petition by Aryan Mining and Trading Corporation against Shevin Capital Services, starting insolvency proceedings. The creditor said it lent Rs 75 lakh in January 2017 and claimed about Rs 1.15 crore with interest once repayment stopped. Shevin Capital denied the sum was a loan, but the bench held that part payments and loan confirmations on record proved the default.
card_tip: A lender relying on part payments and written loan confirmations rather than a signed loan agreement can still establish default for a Section 7 petition if the record supports it.
verification_notes: The admission date of 3 November 2026, the case number C.P.(IB) 54/KB/2026, the financial creditor's name, the Rs 75 lakh principal lent in January 2017, the claimed amount of about Rs 1,14,76,223 and the corporate debtor's denial that the sum was a loan are confirmed from both the Oquilia report and the TaxGuru write-up opened in this run. An NCLT Kolkata cause list from August 2026 independently shows the same case number and parties listed as pending admission, corroborating that the matter was genuinely before the bench. The order itself was not opened. Regional focus: NCLT Kolkata, within the firm's Kolkata practice base.
